details:
My friends and I often engage in late-night VRChat sessions, and sometimes, one of us falls asleep. However, this situation can be problematic as other players may unintentionally disturb my sleeping friend by using disruptive elements like intense light, avatar sound effects, map sound effects, or microphone interference. The awake friend needs to stay vigilant and caution others not to disturb the sleeping player, causing inconvenience for the remaining users trying to sleep peacefully.

I propose allowing users to proactively delegate their safety management to specific friends. In this way, when the designated friend discovers that someone has fallen asleep, they can manually disable the sleeping player's visual and auditory systems to ensure a disturbance-free sleep. A reminder would appear next to the sleeping user's name, indicating that they are under sleep protection and cannot respond to calls unless contacted by someone with admin privileges or a password. The sleeping user's headset display would enter a night mode, and a reminder about the activated sleep protection would be displayed. To exit, a sliding unlock is required to avoid accidental controller touches leading to intense light interference.
title: "I recommend adding an option for sleeping VR players to delegate self-protection to others
